core.text: Commit to selection reordering as the main account: refresh changes the key occupying a retained row, and the editor commits to that current occupant. The stipulated K2-to-K5 miswrite supports this mechanism within the synthetic rules. It does not establish that refresh before every commit is necessary or that mismatch-driven feedback recurs.

Adopt a prospective seven-minute construction retaining row binding: with S0 loaded, inspect/select K2 during 0-1 and commit during 1-2; inspect/select K5 during 2-3 and commit during 3-4; inspect/select K7 during 4-5 and commit during 5-6. Refresh only during 6-7, loading S2. Targets remain fixed while snapshot eligibility advances; no intermediate refresh changes a selected row.

Predicted completion is exactly K2, K5 and K7 checked, all other keys unchecked, zero incorrect-key writes, unchanged read-only scores and final S2 loaded. Validate action times, selected rows, intended and actual written keys, and final statuses by immutable key. Equal scores for K5 and K7 prohibit score-only verification. This outcome is a hypothesis pending replay.

residue.text: Retain the unobserved mismatch-to-refresh return link as a separate hypothesis. Cross changing/frozen snapshots with row/key binding under matched actions, then enable/suppress mismatch-triggered requests. Recurrence requires a return refresh to alter a retained selection; requests alone would not establish repeated miswrites.

Diagnostic arms can produce wrong-key writes and therefore fail the valued outcome even if later repaired. Keep causal diagnostics distinct from the proposed completion schedule; compare every commit, not merely final statuses.

The account is bounded to eight invented records and deterministic timing. Real selection binding, detection and interruption costs are unknown; concurrency, deletion and failed snapshot loads are excluded. No production reliability, operational savings or human benefit follows.

tension.account_a: Necessity hypothesis: reliable correction requires refresh immediately before every commit.
tension.account_b: Selection-reordering hypothesis: retained row identity changes across refresh; fixed-key corrections can succeed without intermediate refresh.
tension.prediction_a: The proposed no-intermediate-refresh schedule cannot satisfy zero wrong-key writes, exact target statuses and final freshness, despite its final refresh.
tension.prediction_b: The same schedule predicts writes only to K2, K5 and K7 and final S2 compliance at minute seven. A verified replay would falsify account A within this model; replay success is not yet observed.
